**Finding submitted: INSURANCE — missing (fallback redline).**

**What I found.** There is no mandatory insurance covenant anywhere in the APCN 2 Construction & Maintenance Agreement:

- **Para 5.3 (p0139)** is purely permissive — each Party *"may"* insure its own share, and joint insurance only happens *"[s]hould the Parties jointly agree"*, with the premium then becoming a Capital Cost.
- **The cost definitions (p0133)** affirmatively bless self-insurance, permitting *"a reasonable allowance in lieu of insurance if such Party elects to carry a risk itself."*
- **Para 5.2 (p0138)** absorbs construction-phase damage or loss into Capital Costs, and **paras 6(a)–(b) (p0141–p0142)** roll third-party claims and damages into O&M Costs.

The combined effect is adverse to us: an uninsured loss on another Party's side is recharged to us through the Capital Cost / O&M Cost sharing mechanics. No minimum limits, no E&O, no cyber, no certificates exist, so the rule fails at every fallback element.

**Target level and why.** I selected the **fallback** (E&O USD 1M, cyber USD 2M) rather than preferred. This is a multilateral consortium cable agreement, not a services or hosting engagement, so I did not volunteer the more onerous preferred limits (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, workers' compensation, certificates on request) — the checklist ceiling rule applies. The preferred package is flagged in the rationale as available if the counterparties will accept it.

**Drafting choices.**
- **Direction guarded.** The covenant binds *"Each Party other than Teleglobe USA Inc."* A symmetric "each Party" covenant would have imposed a brand-new insurance obligation on our own client while completing the element — that weakens the customer and I avoided it.
- **Genuinely absent clause → `insert_after`**, not a rewrite of neighbouring para 5.3. The optional-insurance right in 5.3 is left verbatim; it benefits us as an option and needed no edit.
- **Ceiling respected.** I omitted the model language's "at its own expense", the term-plus-one-year survival tail, and the certificate mechanic, none of which is a selected fallback element.
- The fallback cyber element is unconditional, so no "if Vendor processes Customer Data" trigger (and therefore no Customer Data scoping question) arises here.

Both fallback elements are mapped to operation 1; `propose_redline` returned `ok:true` with the minimality gate clean.
